evidence: app/src/lib/server/pokeapi.ts — all upstream PokeAPI access lives in this single module; every other file consumes the typed domain model
app/src/lib/types.ts:1-71 — clean output boundary: components only see `Card`, `PokemonDetail`, `MoveRow`, etc.
app/src/lib/server/pokeapi.ts:12-15 — spec-derived constants (PAGE_SIZE, MAX_FORM_ID, EXCLUDED_TYPES) centralized in one place
app/src/lib/server/pokeapi.ts:44,59,116-118,215-216 — `api<T = any>` and `as any[]` casts: the upstream input boundary is untyped, so API shape changes surface only at runtime
app/package.json:5-7,19-20 — no devDependencies at all: `typescript` is not installed and no `tsc`/check script exists, so the strict tsconfig (app/tsconfig.json:10) is never verified in CI
app/src/lib/server/pokeapi.ts:133,187 — sprite URLs derived from a hardcoded `/media/sprites/pokemon/<id>.png` pattern instead of API-provided `sprites.front_default`
app/src/routes/index.tsx:5 vs app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].tsx:60-62 — search-param array handling implemented twice, in two different styles
churn_resistance.rationale: Data access is behind one well-defined module with a typed domain model, constants and config are centralized, and no framework internals are relied on — an upgrade would touch few files. The gaps are an untyped input boundary (`any` casts on PokeAPI responses) and the total absence of a typecheck step, which is the main way regressions would slip through as the app ages.

findings.issue: No devDependencies and no typecheck script: `typescript` is not installed, so the `strict` tsconfig is never enforced; vite build does not typecheck, and type regressions would ship silently.
findings.suggestion: Add `typescript` as a devDependency and a `"check": "tsc --noEmit"` script, run in CI alongside the build.

findings.issue: The upstream PokeAPI input boundary is untyped: `api<T = any>` plus `as any[]`/`(p: any)` casts throughout mean changes to API response shapes are invisible to TypeScript, even though the output model is well typed.
findings.suggestion: Define minimal response interfaces for the resources actually consumed (species, pokemon, type, move, ability, generation) and pass them as `api<T>` at each call site.

findings.issue: Upstream fetches have no timeout or `AbortSignal.timeout()`, so a slow or hung PokeAPI request blocks SSR responses indefinitely (Node 24 supports AbortSignal.timeout natively).
findings.suggestion: Pass `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10_000)` to the fetch and translate aborts into a 502-style error.

findings.issue: Server-only-ness of the data layer relies on import discipline (it is only imported inside `"use server"` bodies) rather than the framework's build-time enforcement, which keys on the `.server.` filename suffix.
findings.suggestion: Rename to `src/lib/server/pokeapi.server.ts` (or add `import "@solidjs/start/server-only"`) so a client-side import fails at build time.

findings.issue: Card sprite URLs are derived from a hardcoded `/media/sprites/pokemon/<id>.png` pattern instead of the API's `sprites.front_default`; a change in media layout breaks every card list (the spec does document the pattern, and it avoids 1025 extra fetches, so it is a defensible tradeoff).
findings.suggestion: Keep the pattern but centralize it in one named helper with a comment referencing the spec, so it is a one-line fix if media moves.

findings.issue: Search-param parsing (`params` values can be `string | string[]`) is handled with a local `first()` helper here but re-implemented inline at app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].tsx:60-62, in a different style.
findings.suggestion: Move `first()` into `app/src/lib/format.ts` (or a small `params.ts`) and use it in both routes.

findings.issue: The deployment layer rides nitro's beta channel (`3.0.260903-beta`). It is the latest published version and the one the official migration guide installs, so it is correct today, but it means occasional breaking bumps within the same semver range.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable as-is; consider pinning to a known-good version rather than `^` if build reproducibility ever matters more than updates.

summary: This is a textbook SolidStart v2 app: every framework API in use — `query`/`"use server"`/`createAsync`, `route.preload`, `createHandler({ mode })`, `HttpStatusCode`, the `solidStart()+nitro()` Vite plugin pair — matches the current stable documentation, with no legacy router or vinxi-era constructs left behind. The stack (start 2.1.0, router 1.x, vite 8, nitro 3, node 24) is exactly what the official v2 migration guide prescribes, and the dependency list is the framework's own packages plus nothing else. It ages well architecturally — one server-only data module feeding a typed domain model — but the upstream API responses are untyped (`any` casts) and, more notably, `typescript` isn't even installed, so the strict tsconfig never actually runs, which is the main way this codebase could rot silently.
